true_answer: That is, we fixed the A -element. Broken up this way, we have A × B | ({ a 1 }× B )∪({ a 2 }× B )∪({ a 3 }× B )∪···∪({ a m }× B ) . So A × B is really the union of m disjoint sets. Each of those sets has n elements in them. The total (using the additive principle) is n + n + n + ··· + n | m · n . To summarize: Multiplicative Principle (with sets). Given two sets A and B , we have | A × B | | | A |·| B | . Again, we can easily extend this to any number of sets.
